Q: Find total size of uncommitted or untracked files in git A:

An old question, but the existing answers were slow and flaky, so I came up with this.

git ls-files -mo --exclude-standard | tr '\n' '\0' | du -bc --files0-from=-

Or if you are not interested in the size of every individual file:

git ls-files -mo --exclude-standard | tr '\n' '\0' | du -bc --files0-from=- | tail -n1

Explanation:

  • git ls-files -mo --exclude-standard lists all unstaged modified files (-m) and untracked files (-o) while obeying .gitignore (--exclude-standard)
  • tr '\n' '\0' replaces every newline character by a null character, producing an output similar to that of find -print0
  • du -bc --files0-from=- prints the size of each file, in bytes (-b; disk blocks are irrelevant for git push), followed by a grand total (-c)
  • tail -n1 suppresses the individual files, keeping only the final line of output, which is the total size

Unfortunately, this script will not give you a subtotal per subdirectory. That requires some post-processing. Here's a simple example:

git ls-files -mo --exclude-standard | tr '\n' '\0' | du -b --files0-from=- | awk '{t+=s=$1;gsub(/^[^\t]*\t|[^\/]*$/,"");a[$0]+=s}END{for(f in a)print a[f]"\t"f;print t"\ttotal"}'

Many thanks go to:

  • https://stackoverflow.com/a/32347615
  • https://stackoverflow.com/a/42717225
  • https://blog.jj5.net/blog/2012/01/07/replacing-new-lines-with-nulls-in-bash/

Q: How to get tarot card meanings data in Python? A:

I found a Python package that provides exactly this. Install it with:

  pip install tarot-card-meanings

Basic usage:

  from tarot_card_meanings import get_card, random_card, three_card_spread

  # Get a specific card
  card = get_card("The Star")
  print(card["upright"])   # "Hope, renewal, spirituality"
  print(card["reversed"])  # "Despair, lack of faith"
  print(card["love"])      # "Healing love, renewed hope"
  print(card["career"])    # "Creative inspiration, dream career"
  print(card["yes_no"])    # "Yes"
  print(card["guide"])     # URL to detailed guide

  # Draw a random card
  card = random_card()

  # 3-card spread (Past/Present/Future)
  spread = three_card_spread()
  print(spread["past"]["name"])
  print(spread["present"]["name"])
  print(spread["future"]["name"])

  # Calculate birth card
  birth = birth_card(6, 15, 1992)  # June 15, 1992
  print(birth["name"])  # "The Lovers"

The package includes all 78 cards with 12 data fields each.

The same dataset is also available on:

  • Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/morrispoint/complete-tarot-card-meanings-all-78-cards
  • Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Blacik/tarot-card-meanings-78
  • NPM (for JavaScript): npm install tarot-card-meanings

PyPI page: https://pypi.org/project/tarot-card-meanings/

Q: I want to click a button in Google sheets that will increment cells that have a number by 1 A:

the easiest incrementiation is done by enabling Iterative calculation.

for that, go to:

File > Settings > Calculation > Iterative calculation > On
                              > Max. number of iterations > 1

put a checkbox in B1.

put this formula in A1:

=IF(B1, A1+1, A1+1)

press the checkbox.

if you want to do something more advanced you will need a script

Q: Can We Create SharePoint Custom Web Parts in Office 365 Online with out using Visual Studio? A:

You can create sandbox solutions with SharePoint online.

But in SharePoint 2013 You can do many things just with Content Editor Web Part, javascript and REST services. And with search and display templates. We are using such technics with our on-premise SharePont 2013. And its cover all our needs. Client Object Model and REST services cover almost all SharPoint features. For content processing you can use Content by Search Web Part with display templates. For UI you can use javascript components like JQuery UI.
